Passage I Summary (Q.31–40)
A University College London (UCL) review of brain-imaging studies on 237 volunteers from East Asian countries reports that internet addiction alters multiple neural networks in adolescents, raising activity in some networks while lowering it in others. Researcher Max Chang notes that these connectivity shifts resemble gambling and substance addiction and disrupt systems governing cognitive control, impulsivity, and reward valuation. Affected adolescents may struggle with relationships and social life, lie about online activity, or suffer irregular eating and poor sleep during this crucial developmental stage.

Passage II Summary (Q.41–50)
Calcutta grew into the 'second city of the empire' and the centre of the 'Bengal Renaissance', where modern culture emerged through the interaction of Indian traditions with European contributions. Historian Prof. Sushobhan Sarkar argued that this dialectical influence of British ideas on local traditions caused a profound intellectual awakening, making the term 'renaissance' quite plausible, drawing on Bengali, Sanskrit, and Persian scholarship. Beginning in the late 18th century under Warren Hastings, the Royal Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784) expanded scholarly study of ancient India and European-Indian intellectual exchange. Early 19th-century Calcutta saw new colleges, libraries, systematic legal practice, theatres, and a spirit of progress.
